A first-class litellm provider makes it one command: `pi\n  --provider litellm`. No new provider code, it reuses openai-completions since LiteLLM uses that format.                                                                                                            \n\n\n### How? (optional)\n\nModels registered with api: \"openai-completions\". Base URL defaults to localhost:4000 for local proxies, overridable via LITELLM_BASE_URL for users with hosted or self-managed LiteLLM deployments. Provider display name added for /login flow. Docs in providers.md covering local, hosted, and Docker scenarios. Implementation ready on my fork.","number":4561,"state":"CLOSED","title":"feat(ai): add LiteLLM as API provider","updatedAt":"2026-05-15T15:38:34Z","url":"https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/4561"},{"body":"## Summary\n\n`pi -p \"<prompt>\"` hangs forever (no output, no error, never exits) for **some providers** when stdout/stdin is **not a TTY** (pipe, agent harness, CI). The same command works instantly when wrapped in a pseudo-TTY via `script -qec`. Behavior is provider-dependent: `openai-codex` works fine without a TTY, while `deepseek` and a custom OpenAI-compatible provider hang.\n\n## Environment\n\n- pi 0.79.1 (`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`), Node v22.22.3\n- WSL2 (Ubuntu) on Windows, invoked from an agent harness (Cursor) where stdout is a pipe\n\n## Reproduction\n\n```bash\n# Hangs forever (killed by timeout; zero bytes of output):\ntimeout 60 pi -p \"reply with single word: ok\" \\\n  --provider deepseek --model deepseek-v4-flash \\\n  --no-tools --no-session -ns -np -nc --thinking off\n# => exit 124, no output\n\n# Same command under a pseudo-TTY: responds in ~2 s:\nscript -qec \"pi -p 'reply with single word: ok' \\\n  --provider deepseek --model deepseek-v4-flash \\\n  --no-tools --no-session -ns -np -nc --thinking off\" /dev/null\n# => \"ok\", exit 0\n```\n\nProvider matrix (identical environment, all credentials present in `auth.json`):\n\n| provider | non-TTY `-p` | pseudo-TTY `-p` | interactive TUI |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `openai-codex` (gpt-5.5) | works (~6 s) | works | works |\n| `deepseek` (deepseek-v4-flash) | **hangs forever** | works (~2 s) | works |\n| custom OpenAI-compatible provider | **hangs forever** | works (~2 s) | works |\n\n## Ruled out during diagnosis\n\n- Network/proxy: `curl` reaches `api.deepseek.com` through the same env in 0.11 s (HTTP 401 without key, as expected)\n- Proxy env vars: hang persists both with proxy vars removed and with `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1` (undici `EnvHttpProxyAgent` warning confirms it was active)\n- Credentials: both providers work in the interactive TUI with the same `auth.json`\n- Concurrent pi sessions / lockfiles: no `*.lock` present, no other pi process running\n- `--mode json` makes no difference (still zero output)\n\n## Expected\n\n`-p` should behave the same regardless of whether stdout is a TTY — print the response and exit (or fail fast with an error), for every provider.\n\n## Possibly related\n\n- #4303 (`pi -p --mode json` never exits when stdin is /dev/null) — similar non-TTY trigger, but that one produced output and failed to exit; here nothing is ever emitted and the request seemingly never completes\n- #5571 (`pi -p` hangs with unauthenticated default provider) — here credentials are present and the same provider works in the TUI\n\nHappy to provide verbose logs or bisect further if you point me at a debug flag.\n","number":5628,"state":"CLOSED","title":"pi -p hangs forever for some providers (deepseek, custom OpenAI-compatible) when stdout is not a TTY; pseudo-TTY wrapper fixes it","updatedAt":"2026-06-11T13:43:32Z","url":"https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/5628"},{"body":"### Bug Description\n\nWhen registering a custom provider via `pi.registerProvider()` in an extension, the **provider-level** `compat` object is silently ignored for each model. Only the **model-level** `compat` is used.\n\nThis causes a 400 error (`developer is not one of ['system', 'assistant', 'user', 'tool', 'function']`) when the target API does not support the `developer` role, even though `supportsDeveloperRole: false` is correctly set at the provider level.\n\n### Reproduction\n\n1. Create an extension that registers a custom OpenAI-compatible provider with provider-level compat:\n\n```typescript\nconst SHARED_COMPAT = {\n  supportsDeveloperRole: false,\n  maxTokensField: \"max_tokens\" as const,\n};\n\npi.registerProvider(\"my-provider\", {\n  name: \"My Provider\",\n  baseUrl: \"https://api.example.com/v1\",\n  apiKey: \"$MY_API_KEY\",\n  api: \"openai-completions\",\n  compat: SHARED_COMPAT,\n  models: [\n    {\n      id: \"my-model\",\n      name: \"My Model\",\n      reasoning: true,\n      input: [\"text\"],\n      contextWindow: 128000,\n      maxTokens: 4096,\n      cost: { input: 0, output: 0, cacheRead: 0, cacheWrite: 0 },\n    },\n  ],\n});\n```\n\n2. Start pi and send any message.\n3. **Expected:** The system prompt is sent with `role: \"system\"` (per `supportsDeveloperRole: false`).\n4. **Actual:** The system prompt is sent with `role: \"developer\"`, causing a 400 error from the API.\n\n### Root Cause Analysis\n\nIn `dist/core/model-registry.js`, there are two code paths that resolve a model's `compat`:\n\n**Path 1 — `models.json` loading (correct):**\n\n```javascript\n// ~line 495\nconst compat = mergeCompat(providerConfig.compat, modelDef.compat);\n```\n\nThis correctly merges provider-level compat into each model.\n\n**Path 2 — `registerProvider()` runtime (buggy):**\n\n```javascript\n// ~line 760, inside applyProviderConfig()\nthis.models.push({\n  id: modelDef.id,\n  name: modelDef.name,\n  api: api,\n  provider: providerName,\n  baseUrl: modelDef.baseUrl ?? config.baseUrl,\n  reasoning: modelDef.reasoning,\n  thinkingLevelMap: modelDef.thinkingLevelMap,\n  input: modelDef.input,\n  cost: modelDef.cost,\n  contextWindow: modelDef.contextWindow,\n  maxTokens: modelDef.maxTokens,\n  headers: undefined,\n  compat: modelDef.compat,  // ← BUG: provider-level config.compat is not merged\n});\n```\n\nOnly `modelDef.compat` is used; `config.compat` (the provider-level compat) is completely ignored.\n\n### Workaround\n\nExplicitly set `compat` on each model definition:\n\n```typescript\nmodels: [\n  {\n    id: \"my-model\",\n    // ...\n    compat: { ...SHARED_COMPAT },  // duplicate per model\n  },\n],\n```\n\nThis works but is verbose and error-prone when registering many models with shared compat settings.\n\n### Suggested Fix\n\nIn `applyProviderConfig()`, merge provider-level compat with model-level compat when pushing models:\n\n```javascript\ncompat: mergeCompat(config.compat, modelDef.compat),\n```\n\nThis would make the `registerProvider()` path consistent with the `models.json` loading path.\n\n### Environment\n\n- pi version: latest (via npm)\n- OS: Linux\n- API type: `openai-completions` with a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint\n","number":5349,"state":"CLOSED","title":"registerProvider() ignores provider-level compat, causing developer role errors","updatedAt":"2026-06-04T21:44:11Z","url":"https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/5349"},{"body":"### What happened?\n\nWhen attempting to route traffic through a custom OpenAI-compatible proxy (such as Ultimate AI) by overriding the baseUrl of the native \"openai\" provider in models.json, the agent hard-crashes immediately upon sending the first prompt. The native handler fails to parse the proxy's stream correctly, resulting in an unhandled .push error on the session's summary object.\n\n### Steps to reproduce\n\nEnsure you are running Pi version 0.76.0.\n\nConfigure ~/.pi/agent/models.json to override the built-in openai provider:\n\nJSON\n{\n  \"providers\": {\n    \"openai\": {\n      \"baseUrl\": \"https://chat.ultimateai.org/v1\"\n    }\n  }\n}\nAuthenticate the provider (either via auth.json or by injecting the API key).\n\nLaunch the agent in the termina…15166 tokens truncated…en in current llama.cpp)\n    - reasoning model?\n    - \"image\" input?\n4. Add \"llamacpp\" provider with available models\n\nOne complication is that llama-server loads a model into memory before answering `/props` queries, this means pi has incomplete metadata for unloaded models.\n\nA \"before_provider_request\" handler can set the `llama-server` specific parameters:\n- chat template\n    - `enable_thinking`\n    - `reasoning_effort` (when applicable)\n- thinking budget for reasoning models\n    - derived from max tokens and pi thinking level\n    - as mentioned in https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/issues/3208#issuecomment-4276319082\n\nRough extension: https://gist.github.com/pyfisch/31831b77a3a18275b21aa22f3880f353\nIf approved I will send a PR.","number":3567,"state":"CLOSED","title":"Official llama.cpp provider","updatedAt":"2026-05-12T14:34:07Z","url":"https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/3567"},{"body":"## What do you want to change?\n\nImplement or remove the documented `pi agent` command in `packages/pods`.\n\n`packages/pods/README.md`, `pi --help`, and `pi start` output all present `pi agent <name> ...` as the chat path for a started pod model. The CLI routes that command to `promptModel()`, but `promptModel()` builds the agent arguments and then unconditionally throws:\n\n```ts\nthrow new Error(\"Not implemented\");\n```\n\n## Why?\n\nThe command is advertised as the next step after starting a model, but it always exits with `Agent error: Not implemented` once a configured model is found.\n\nMinimal repro without a real pod:\n\n```bash\ntmpdir=$(mktemp -d)\ncat > \"$tmpdir/pods.json\" <<'JSON'\n{\"active\":\"local\",\"pods\":{\"local\":{\"ssh\":\"ssh root@127.0.0.1\",\"gpus\":[],\"models\":{\"qwen\":{\"model\":\"Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct\",\"port\":8001,\"gpu\":[],\"pid\":12345}}}}}\nJSON\nPI_CONFIG_DIR=\"$tmpdir\" PI_API_KEY=dummy npx tsx packages/pods/src/cli.ts agent qwen \"hello\"\n```\n\nOutput:\n\n```text\nAgent error: Not implemented\n```\n\n## How? (optional)\n\nWire `promptModel()` to the agent entry point using the base URL/model/API key arguments it already constructs, or remove the `pi agent` command and docs until that integration exists.\n\nVersion: `main` at `0fce64d4`\n","number":3626,"state":"CLOSED","title":"pkg:pods: documented pi agent command always exits with Not implemented","updatedAt":"2026-04-24T01:02:47Z","url":"https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/3626"},{"body":"### What happened?\n\nAuto-compaction still has no reliable mid-turn backpressure. In a long tool loop, context can grow past the configured `contextWindow` before pi checks compaction, because each successful assistant/tool turn can append large tool results and immediately start the next LLM call.\n\nThis is notable architecturally: `contextWindow` is the only model/runtime budget available to custom providers, local providers, proxies, and extensions. If the agent loop does not enforce it at the loop boundary, the provider becomes the context-control mechanism. That is reactive, provider-specific, and can waste the successful work from the oversized request. For custom providers where the configured `contextWindow` is lower than the upstream hard limit, pi can silently run far beyond the configured budget.\n\nCurrent `main` still has the gap:\n\n- `AgentLoopConfig.shouldStopAfterTurn` exists and `agent-loop.ts` calls it after `turn_end`.\n- `Agent` does not expose `shouldStopAfterTurn` in `AgentOptions`, does not store it, and does not pass it through `createLoopConfig()`.\n- `coding-agent` does not wire this hook for compaction.\n- `_checkCompaction()` runs after `agent.prompt()`/`agent.continue()` settles and before a new user prompt, not before each LLM call in a tool loop.\n- On successful assistant messages, `_checkCompaction()` uses `calculateContextTokens(assistantMessage.usage)`, which reflects the request before appended tool results. It does not include the tool results that will be sent on the next LLM call.\n\nRelated prior issues: #1796, #1884, #2871, #3660, #4325. Related provider/custom-context failures: #4497, #4563, #4608, #4943. Related post-compaction continuation failures: #5056, #5120, #5212, #5420, #5463.\n\n### Steps to reproduce\n\n1. Configure a custom/OpenAI-compatible provider model with a `contextWindow` lower than the provider's real accepted limit, for example `contextWindow: 200000`.\n2. Enable auto-compaction with a reserve, for example `reserveTokens: 16000`.\n3. Start a session near but below the threshold.\n4. Ask pi to do work that repeatedly reads or produces large tool outputs in one agent run.\n5. Observe that tool results push the next request above the configured threshold/window, but no compaction happens until the full agent run ends or the provider rejects/overflows.\n\nThe deterministic code path is: assistant usage is below threshold, tool results are appended, the loop continues, and the next provider request is made without a compaction check that includes those appended tool results.\n\n### Expected behavior\n\n`contextWindow` should be enforceable as an agent-loop invariant, not only as a post-run or provider-error recovery signal.\n\nA robust design would:\n\n- expose `shouldStopAfterTurn` on `Agent` and pass it through to `AgentLoopConfig`;\n- in coding-agent, use it to estimate current context after tool results and stop cleanly before the next LLM call when `shouldCompact()` is true;\n- have the existing auto-compaction path compact and resume the tool loop;\n- optionally keep a pre-request guard after context transforms/steering/follow-ups so an oversized request is never sent.\n\nThis avoids unbounded context growth in long tool-call sequences and makes custom provider `contextWindow` settings meaningful.\n\n### Version\n\n`main` at 35120d7e. Also observed in released 0.73.x–0.78.x behavior via the linked issues.","number":5512,"state":"CLOSED","title":"Auto-compaction has no mid-turn context guard, so long tool loops can exceed configured contextWindow","updatedAt":"2026-06-09T10:00:33Z","url":"https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/5512"},{"body":"## What happened?\n\nPrompt caching does not work when using the `openai-responses` API path with non-OpenAI providers (proxies like theclawbay, litellm, etc.). The server-side cache routing headers `session_id` and `x-client-request-id` are never sent, so every request is a cache miss.\n\nThree issues in `packages/ai/src/providers/`:\n\n1. **openai-responses.ts:181** — `session_id` and `x-client-request-id` headers are gated behind `model.provider === \"openai\" && model.baseUrl.includes(\"api.openai.com\")`. I am requesting the ability to add the resource name to `auth.json`.\n\n### Why?\n\n- Keeps ALL required secrets and configuration in a single place (the `auth.json` file).\n- Parity with API key settings: you can already put keys and even shell commands or ENV references inside `auth.json`.\n- Many organizations use several Azure resources and would benefit from being able to set the correct resource (and rotate it) in a versioned config file rather than via env var.\n\n### How? This keeps the `auth.json` format self-contained for Azure like for other providers.","number":3219,"state":"CLOSED","title":"Feature request: Support setting Azure resourceName in auth.json for azure-openai-responses","updatedAt":"2026-04-15T11:32:18Z","url":"https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/3219"},{"body":"## Bug\n\nIn `--mode rpc`, the **first prompt** always returns `success: false` with:\n\n```\n{\"type\":\"response\",\"command\":\"prompt\",\"success\":false,\"error\":\"Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'startsWith')\"}\n```\n\nThe **second prompt** (and all subsequent ones) works fine:\n\n```\n{\"type\":\"response\",\"command\":\"prompt\",\"success\":true}\n```\n\nThis affects **all models** (Claude, Gemini, Qwen, custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints) — not model-specific.\n\n## Reproduction\n\n```bash\necho '{\"type\":\"prompt\",\"content\":\"say hi\"}' | pi --mode rpc --provider anthropic --model claude-haiku-4-5\n```\n\n**Output:**\n```json\n{\"type\":\"response\",\"command\":\"prompt\",\"success\":false,\"error\":\"Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'startsWith')\"}\n{\"type\":\"response\",\"command\":\"prompt\",\"success\":true}\n```\n\nFull reproduction script: https://gist.github.com/louis030195/b0c3ece9dff99bb726772d4145c6a693\n\n## Expected\n\nFirst prompt should return `success: true` with streamed content.\n\n## Impact\n\nApplications that embed Pi in RPC mode (like [screenpipe](https://github.com/screenpipe/screenpipe)) see the first `success: false` and show \"No response from model\" to the user. The chat appears broken even though the second attempt would succeed.\n\n## Environment\n\n- `@mariozechner/pi-coding-agent` v0.60.0\n- macOS 15.4 (Darwin 25.2.0)\n- Bun 1.3.7\n- Tested with: Anthropic (claude-haiku-4-5), OpenAI-compatible (qwen/qwen3.5-flash), Gemini","number":2461,"state":"CLOSED","title":"RPC mode: first prompt always fails with 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading startsWith)'","updatedAt":"2026-03-24T00:48:38Z","url":"https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/2461"},{"body":"### What do you want to change?\n\n`packages/ai/src/providers/openai-codex-responses.ts` currently assumes the bearer token is always an official ChatGPT/Codex JWT.\n\nIt calls `extractAccountId()` unconditionally and always sends `chatgpt-account-id`.\n\nI want to keep that behavior for official ChatGPT/OpenAI Codex endpoints, but not for non-official Codex-compatible base URLs.\n\nFor non-official backends, the provider should:\n\n- allow opaque bearer tokens\n- only send `chatgpt-account-id` when account-id extraction actually succeeded\n\n### Why?\n\nThis blocks compatibility layers like [`codex-lb`](https://github.com/Soju06/codex-lb).\n\n`codex-lb` can expose a Codex-compatible `/backend-api/codex` endpoint while using its own bearer keys (for example `sk-clb-...`) for auth, routing, or account pooling. `0.75.5`\n- Node: `v22.22.1`\n- Provider/model: `openai-codex` / `gpt-5.5`\n- Thinking level: `xhigh`\n- No explicit `transport` setting in user settings\n- Default tools/extensions enabled\n\n## Observed behavior\n\nWhen the issue occurs:\n\n- TUI keeps showing `Working...` for minutes.\n- No assistant text is streamed.\n- No tool call is emitted.\n- Pressing Escape aborts the turn.\n- The   \"cacheRead\": 0,\n    \"cacheWrite\": 0,\n    \"totalTokens\": 0\n  }\n}\n```\n\nI saw this pattern multiple times, including cases where the previous turn had completed normally and the next user Optionally show a clearer status/error when a provider turn has produced zero events for a long time.\n\nLocal workaround I am considering, but have not applied yet:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"transport\": \"sse\",\n  \"httpIdleTimeoutMs\": 120000\n}\n```\n\nI can provide more sanitized session metadata if helpful, but I avoided attaching raw session logs because they contain private conversation/tool context.\n","number":4945,"state":"OPEN","title":"openai-codex Connection Reliability Issues","updatedAt":"2026-06-16T07:35:03Z","url":"https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/4945"},{"body":"### What happened?\n\n[The documentation](https://pi.dev/docs/latest/models#openai-compatibility) states that\n> For providers with partial OpenAI compatibility, use the compat field.\n> \\<snip\\>\n> | Field | Description |\n> | --- | --- |\n> | `openRouterRouting` | OpenRouter provider routing preferences. <br> **This object is sent as-is in the provider field of the OpenRouter API request.** |\n\nHowever, in reality the `provider` field is only sent if `baseUrl` contains `\"openrouter.ai\"`:\nhttps://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/ea3465a8e371a12d0167a06b60f93878e3a3df44/packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.ts#L613\n\nThere are cases, when `baseUrl` could be different from `\"openrouter.ai\"`, but sending the `provider` field should still be sent:\n\n1) Some LLM providers support many options from the OpenRouter API extensions (including the `provider` object), not just the `ai-sdk/openai-compatible` subset.\n\n2) It's possible that `baseUrl` points to a proxy / gateway of some kind that eventually forwards the requests to `openrouter.ai`. ]\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    ```\n\n3) Observe the fact that `pi` silently ignores the `openRouterRouting` key (no `provider` object is inserted into the requests).\n\n### Expected As noted in #5338, a separate provider is required.\n\n## Why?\n\nAWS is rolling out a class of models on the Bedrock Mantle endpoint that cannot be used through the existing `amazon-bedrock` provider. Without this provider, those models are permanently inaccessible in pi.\n\n## How?\n\n- New provider `amazon-bedrock-mantle` in `packages/ai`, wired to the OpenAI-compatible Bedrock Mantle endpoint\n- Auth via AWS credential chain (SigV4), targeting `bedrock-mantle.{region}.api.aws`\n- `openai.gpt-5.4` and `openai.gpt-5.5` hard-coded in the model catalog for now; `models.dev` does not yet track these models (see [anomalyco/models.dev#1962](https://github.com/anomalyco/models.dev/issues/1962))","number":5363,"state":"OPEN","title":"Add amazon-bedrock-mantle provider for OpenAI-compatible models","updatedAt":"2026-06-15T13:23:07Z","url":"https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/5363"},{"body":"### What happened?\n\nBehind a proxy/gateway, when an endpoint returns a non-2xx with a body the SDK can't parse into its schema, most providers drop the body. The same 403 surfaces differently per provider:\n\n- Bedrock → `Unknown: UnknownError`\n- OpenAI completions → `403 status code (no body)`\n- Gemini / Vertex / Codex Responses → the SDK's opaque message\n- OpenAI / Azure Responses → status shown, body dropped\n- Anthropic, Mistral → the real reason (correct)\n\nEach provider builds `output.errorMessage` from `error.message` (some add a status code), never falling back to the raw body the SDK still carries. `formatMistralError` (`packages/ai/src/providers/mistral.ts`) already reads `sdkError.statusCode` + `sdkError.body` — that's the pattern everyone should use.\n\nAffected files: `amazon-bedrock.ts`, `openai-completions.ts`, `google.ts`, `google-vertex.ts`, `openai-codex-responses.ts` (body-blind); `openai-responses.ts`, `azure-openai-responses.ts` (status-only). Anthropic works only because its SDK folds the body into `error.message`.\n\n### Steps to reproduce\n\n1. Put any OpenAI-compatible / Bedrock-Converse / Gemini proxy in front that returns `403` with `{\"error\":\"<reason>\"}`.\n2. Point pi at it and send a request it rejects.\n3. The surfaced error is opaque (`Unknown: UnknownError`, `403 status code (no body)`, etc.) instead of the reason in the body.\n\n### Expected behavior\n\nWhen the SDK parses the body into `error.message`, keep showing that. Otherwise fall back to HTTP status + raw body — e.g. `403: {\"error\":\"<reason>\"}` — the way Mistral already does. Cleanest as one shared helper all `catch` blocks route through. I'm happy to implement this; no new dependency (the fields already exist on the SDK error objects).\n\nHappy to implement the fix myself if you lgtm.\n\n### Version\n\n0.79.1","number":5763,"state":"OPEN","title":"Providers swallow the HTTP error body, so gateway / non-schema errors are unreadable","updatedAt":"2026-06-17T07:30:11Z","url":"https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/5763"},{"body":"### What happened?\n\noptions.maxTokens in pi-ai is silently ignored for opencode-go provider. The API accepts max_tokens but pi-ai sends max_completion_tokens, which the backend ignores.\n\n### Steps to reproduce\n\n Send streamSimple(model, ctx, { maxTokens: 1 }) for any opencode-go model  -- output is not truncated.\n\n### Expected behavior\n\nmaxTokens maps to \"max_tokens\", not \"max_completion_tokens\"\n\n### Version\n\n0.78.0","number":5331,"state":"CLOSED","title":"options.maxTokens in pi-ai maps to wrong API parameter for opencode-go provider","updatedAt":"2026-06-09T11:41:23Z","url":"https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/5331"},{"body":"### What happened?\n\nComponent: @earendil-works/pi-ai — providers/openai-completions.js and providers/openai-completions.ts\n\n### Description\n\n When using an OpenAI-compatible provider (LM Studio, Ollama, vLLM, local llama.cpp, etc.), the maxTokens value set in models.json is silently ignored. The buildParams() function only sends max_tokens/max_completion_tokens when options?.maxTokens is\n truthy, but the agent loop never sets options.maxTokens — it only passes the model object reference. The Anthropic provider has the correct fallback: options?.maxTokens ?? model.maxTokens.\n\n Impact: The API receives no output token limit, so the server applies its default (often 512–2048 for llama.cpp-based servers). Long tool calls (e.g., write with >5k tokens of content) get truncated mid-JSON, causing parse failures and incomplete\n writes.\n\n ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n ### Root Cause\n\n Two issues in openai-completions.js:\n\n 1. Missing model.maxTokens fallback in buildParams() (~line 401):\n\n ```js\n   // ❌ Current: only checks options.maxTokens, no fallback to model.maxTokens\n   if (options?.maxTokens) {\n       if (compat.maxTokensField === \"max_tokens\") {\n           params.max_tokens = options.maxTokens;\n       } else {\n           params.max_completion_tokens = options.maxTokens;\n       }\n   }\n ```\n\n Compare with the Anthropic provider (anthropic.js:664):\n\n ```js\n   // ✅ Has fallback\n   max_tokens: options?.maxTokens ?? model.maxTokens,\n ```\n\n 2. No detection of local/private servers in detectCompat() (~line 895). The useMaxTokens boolean only triggers for known SaaS providers:\n\n ```js\n   const useMaxTokens = baseUrl.includes(\"chutes.ai\") || isMoonshot || isCloudflareAiGateway || isTogether;\n ```\n\n Local servers (LM Studio, Ollama, llama.cpp, vLLM) use llama.cpp's OpenAI-compatible API which only understands max_tokens, not max_completion_tokens. Without detection, they get the wrong field name (max_completion_tokens instead of max_tokens).\n\n Data flow trace:\n\n ```\n   models.json → model.maxTokens = 65572 ✅ stored correctly\n   agent.js (createLoopConfig) → does not include maxTokens in config ⚠️\n   agent-loop.js (streamAssistantResponse) → ...config → options.maxTokens = undefined ⚠️\n   openai-completions.js (buildParams) → if (options?.maxTokens) → SKIPPED ❌\n ```\n\n ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n ### Fix\n\n In openai-completions.js, buildParams(): Replace:\n\n ```js\n   if (options?.maxTokens) {\n ```\n\n with:\n\n ```js\n   const effectiveMaxTokens = options?.maxTokens ?? model.maxTokens;\n   if (effectiveMaxTokens) {\n ```\n\n In openai-completions.js, detectCompat(): Add local server detection to useMaxTokens:\n\n ```js\n   const isLocalServer = baseUrl.includes(\"localhost\") || baseUrl.includes(\"127.0.0.1\") || baseUrl.includes(\"10.\") || baseUrl.includes(\"192.168.\");\n   const useMaxTokens = ...existing... || isLocalServer;\n ```\n\n Or, alternatively, make the maxTokensField detection broader — any server that isn't a known OpenAI/OpenAI-compatible SaaS endpoint should default to max_tokens since that's the universally supported field name.\n\n For the TypeScript source (openai-completions.ts), the same changes apply.\n\n ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n ### Workaround\n\n Users can work around issue #2 (wrong field name) by setting explicit compat on their provider:\n\n ```json\n   \"compat\": { \"maxTokensField\": \"max_tokens\" }\n ```\n\n But issue #1 (missing fallback) cannot be worked around without patching the source.\n\n ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n ### Environment\n\n - pi version: @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent latest (as of June 2026)\n - Model: LM Studio with google/gemma-4-e4b, contextWindow/maxTokens configured at 65572\n - API type: openai-completions\n\n### Steps to reproduce\n\n1. Configure a local LM Studio provider in ~/.pi/agent/models.json:\n ```json\n   {\n     \"providers\": {\n       \"lmstudio\": {\n         \"baseUrl\": \"http://localhost:1234/v1\",\n         \"api\": \"openai-completions\",\n         \"apiKey\": \"lm-studio\",\n         \"models\": [\n           { \"id\": \"my-model\", \"contextWindow\": 65572, \"maxTokens\": 65572 }\n         ]\n       }\n     }\n   }\n ```\n\n 2. Set the model in pi (/model). Set thinking to off.\n 3. Ask it to write a ~10,000 character file.\n 4. Expected: File is written successfully.\n 5. Actual: The write tool call is truncated mid-JSON. Server returns finish_reason: \"length\" with incomplete content.\n\n Verified with LM Studio running google/gemma-4-e4b.\n\n### Expected behavior\n\nThe maxTokens value configured in models.json should be sent to the OpenAI-compatible API as either max_tokens or max_completion_tokens (depending on the provider's compatibility). The model should be able to generate up to the configured number of\n output tokens.\n\n Concretely, for the example above:\n\n - Given \"maxTokens\": 65572 in the model config\n - When pi sends the API request to LM Studio\n - Then the request should include \"max_tokens\": 65572\n - And a 10,000-character write should complete without truncation\n\n### Version\n\n_No response_","number":5375,"state":"CLOSED","title":"OpenAI Completions provider ignores model.maxTokens — no fallback when options.maxTokens is undefined","updatedAt":"2026-06-03T21:22:29Z","url":"https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/5375"},{"body":"### Summary\n\n`@earendil-works/pi-ai` already supports OpenAI's `service_tier` request parameter (priority/flex) on the Responses API path, including tier-based cost multipliers — but the coding agent never sets `options.serviceTier` and exposes no config sur…293 tokens truncated… per-model `serviceTier?: \"auto\" | \"default\" | \"flex\" | \"priority\" | \"scale\"` field in `modelOverrides` / `ProviderModelConfig` (and/or a provider-level default, and/or a runtime toggle), so the existing pi-ai capability — including its tier-aware cost accounting — becomes reachable for `openai-responses` / `openai-codex-responses` models.\n\n### Version\n\n`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` 0.79.6 (bundled `@earendil-works/pi-ai` 0.79.6).\n","number":5840,"state":"CLOSED","title":"Expose OpenAI service_tier (priority/flex) from coding-agent config","updatedAt":"2026-06-17T12:59:58Z","url":"https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/5840"},{"body":"### What happened?\n\n`pi.registerProvider()` ignores `models[].baseUrl` and always applies the provider-level `baseUrl` to all registered models.\n\nThis is inconsistent with:  \n   - the exposed type (`ProviderConfigInput.models[].baseUrl` exists), and\n   - `models.json` behavior (which supports per-model `baseUrl`).\n\nIn `packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-registry.ts`, `applyProviderConfig()` currently sets: `baseUrl: config.baseUrl!`  for every model, instead of using `modelDef.baseUrl` when provided.\n\nI am working on a plugin for axonhub which is a model hub providing different models in different base url.\n\n### Steps to reproduce\n\n\n1. Running rm -rf ~/.pi/agent/sessions/ and launching with --session-id fresh-start results in the exact same crash.\n\n\n### Version\n\nv0.76.0 and v0.75.5","number":5125,"state":"CLOSED","title":"bug: Error: currentItem.summary.push is not a function when overriding native openai provider baseUrl","updatedAt":"2026-05-28T11:41:29Z","url":"https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/5125"},{"body":"### What happened?\n\nDuring `/login litellm`, the login dialog prompts for the LiteLLM base URL and then for the API key. When typing into the API-key prompt, the same text is also rendered in the earlier base-URL prompt row.\n\nThe underlying values are captured sequentially, but the UI is misleading and visually leaks the active prompt value into a previous prompt slot.\n\n### Steps to reproduce\n\n1. Run `/login litellm`.\n2. Enter a LiteLLM base URL and submit it.\n3. Start typing the API key in the next prompt.\n4. > AGENT

Yes, but not as an open exact issue.

The closest upstream issue is [earendil-works/pi#8: “Add support for setting base URLs”](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/8). It specifically asks for `OPENAI_BASE_URL=<custom_openai_base_url>` and a custom OpenAI base URL. It is closed. The maintainer resolved it by supporting custom providers/model config, not by adding `OPENAI_BASE_URL` or `--base-url` to the built-in `openai` CLI provider. ([github.com](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/8?utm_source=openai))

I did not find an open issue specifically saying: “`pi --provider openai` should support `OPENAI_BASE_URL` / `--base-url`.”

Related but not exact:

- [#4561](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/4561) added/requested LiteLLM as a first-class OpenAI-compatible provider with `LITELLM_BASE_URL`. ([github.com](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/4561?utm_source=openai))
- [#3196](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/3196) covers behavior for OpenAI-compatible proxies on the `openai-responses` path, but not CLI base URL selection. ([github.com](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/3196?utm_source=openai))

So if we want clean `pi-cli` support for WTG’s OpenAI-compatible endpoint via `subprovider: openai`, we should raise a new narrow upstream issue: add `--base-url` and/or `OPENAI_BASE_URL` support for the built-in OpenAI provider in `pi` CLI.

we can have openai as a custom provider

> AGENT

Yes, but with a specific meaning.

Pi’s closed “base URLs” issue means: Pi supports custom base URLs through its custom provider/model config system. It does not mean `pi --provider openai` automatically honors `OPENAI_BASE_URL`.

So for `pi-cli`, these are different:

```yaml
# Not cleanly supported today by Pi CLI / AgentV
provider: pi-cli
subprovider: openai
base_url: ${{ OPENAI_ENDPOINT }}
```

versus:

```json
// Pi custom provider config, supported by Pi
{
  "providers": {
    "wtg-openai": {
      "baseUrl": "https://.../v1",
      "api": "openai-responses",
      "apiKey": "$OPENAI_API_KEY",
      "models": [
        { "id": "gpt-5.5", "...": "metadata required by Pi" }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Then AgentV could point `pi-cli` at it:

```yaml
- name: pi
  provider: pi-cli
  subprovider: wtg-openai
  api_key: ${{ OPENAI_API_KEY }}
  model: ${{ OPENAI_MODEL }}
  grader_target: grader
```

But that requires the Pi custom provider to exist in Pi’s config or an extension before AgentV runs. AgentV does not currently synthesize that custom provider from `base_url` in a `pi-cli` target.

So: yes, custom provider is viable. But no, it is not the same as “use built-in `openai` subprovider with `base_url` directly” for `pi-cli`. For PR 714, `pi-sdk` can use `subprovider: openai` directly; `pi-cli` needs either `subprovider: azure` as today or a Pi custom provider setup.

   120	
   121	## Supported APIs
   122	
   123	| API | Description |
   124	|-----|-------------|
   125	| `openai-completions` | OpenAI Chat Completions (most compatible) |
   126	| `openai-responses` | OpenAI Responses API |
   127	| `anthropic-messages` | Anthropic Messages API |
   128	| `google-generative-ai` | Google Generative AI |
   129	
   130	Set `api` at provider level (default for all models) or model level (override per model).
   131	
   132	## Provider Configuration
   133	
   134	| Field | Description |
   135	|-------|-------------|
   136	| `baseUrl` | API endpoint URL |
   137	| `api` | API type (see above) |
   138	| `apiKey` | API key (see value resolution below) |
   139	| `headers` | Custom headers (see value resolution below) |
   140	| `authHeader` | Set `true` to add `Authorization: Bearer <apiKey>` automatically |
   141	| `models` | Array of model configurations |
   142	| `modelOverrides` | Per-model overrides for built-in models on this provider |
   143	
   144	### Value Resolution
   145	
   146	The `apiKey` and `headers` fields support command execution, environment interpolation, and literals:
   147	
   148	- **Shell command:** `"!command"` at the start executes the whole value as a command and uses stdout
   149	  ```json
   150	  "apiKey": "!security find-generic-password -ws 'anthropic'"
   151	  "apiKey": "!op read 'op://vault/item/credential'"
   152	  ```
   153	- **Environment interpolation:** `"$ENV_VAR"` or `"${ENV_VAR}"` uses the value of the named variable. Interpolation works inside larger literals.
   154	  ```json
   155	  "apiKey": "$MY_API_KEY"
   156	  "apiKey": "${KEY_PREFIX}_${KEY_SUFFIX}"
   157	  ```
   158	  `$FOO_BAR` is the variable `FOO_BAR`; use `${FOO}_BAR` when `BAR` is literal text. Missing environment variables make the value unresolved.
   159	- **Escapes:** `"$$"` emits a literal `"$"`; `"$!"` emits a literal `"!"` without triggering command execution.
   160	  ```json
   161	  "apiKey": "$$literal-dollar-prefix"
   162	  "apiKey": "$!literal-bang-prefix"
   163	  ```
   164	- **Literal value:** Used directly. Plain uppercase strings such as `MY_API_KEY` are literals; use `$MY_API_KEY` for environment variables.
   165	  ```json
   166	  "apiKey": "sk-..."
   167	  ```
   168	
   169	For `models.json`, shell commands are resolved at request time. pi intentionally does not apply built-in TTL, stale reuse, or recovery logic for arbitrary commands. Different commands need different caching and failure strategies, and pi cannot infer the right one.
   170	
   171	If your command is slow, expensive, rate-limited, or should keep using a previous value on transient failures, wrap it in your own script or command that implements the caching or TTL behavior you want.
   172	
   173	`/model` availability checks use configured auth presence and do not execute shell commands.
   174	
   175	### Custom Headers
   176	
   177	```json
   178	{
   179	  "providers": {
   180	    "custom-proxy": {
   181	      "baseUrl": "https://proxy.example.com/v1",
   182	      "apiKey": "$MY_API_KEY",
   183	      "api": "anthropic-messages",
   184	      "headers": {
   185	        "x-portkey-api-key": "$PORTKEY_API_KEY",
   186	        "x-secret": "!op read 'op://vault/item/secret'"
   187	      },
   188	      "models": [...]
   189	    }
   190	  }
   191	}
   192	```
   193	
   194	## Model Configuration
   195	
   196	| Field | Required | Default | Description |
   197	|-------|----------|---------|-------------|
   198	| `id` | Yes | — | Model identifier (passed to the API) |
   199	| `name` | No | `id` | Human-readable model label. Used for matching (`--model` patterns) and shown as secondary model detail text. |
   200	| `api` | No | provider's `api` | Override provider's API for this model |
   201	| `reasoning` | No | `false` | Supports extended thinking |
   202	| `thinkingLevelMap` | No | omitted | Maps pi thinking levels to provider values and marks unsupported levels (see below) |
   203	| `input` | No | `["text"]` | Input types: `["text"]` or `["text", "image"]` |
   204	| `contextWindow` | No | `128000` | Context window size in tokens |
   205	| `maxTokens` | No | `16384` | Maximum output tokens |
   206	| `cost` | No | all zeros | `{"input": 0, "output": 0, "cacheRead": 0, "cacheWrite": 0}` (per million tokens) |
   207	| `compat` | No | provider `compat` | Provider compatibility overrides. Merged with provider-level `compat` when both are set. |
   208	
   209	Current behavior:
   210	- `/model`, `--list-models`, and the interactive footer display entries by model `id`.
    30	
    31	## Quick Reference
    32	
    33	```typescript
    34	import type { ExtensionAPI } from "@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent";
    35	
    36	export default function (pi: ExtensionAPI) {
    37	  // Override baseUrl for existing provider
    38	  pi.registerProvider("anthropic", {
    39	    baseUrl: "https://proxy.example.com"
    40	  });
    41	
    42	  // Register new provider with models
    43	  pi.registerProvider("my-provider", {
    44	    name: "My Provider",
    45	    baseUrl: "https://api.example.com",
    46	    apiKey: "$MY_API_KEY",
    47	    api: "openai-completions",
    48	    models: [
    49	      {
    50	        id: "my-model",
    51	        name: "My Model",
    52	        reasoning: false,
    53	        input: ["text", "image"],
    54	        cost: { input: 0, output: 0, cacheRead: 0, cacheWrite: 0 },
    55	        contextWindow: 128000,
    56	        maxTokens: 4096
    57	      }
    58	    ]
    59	  });
    60	}
    61	```
    62	
    63	The extension factory can also be `async`. For dynamic model discovery, fetch and register models in the factory instead of `session_start`. pi waits for the factory before startup continues, so the provider is available during interactive startup and to `pi --list-models`.
    64	
    65	## Override Existing Provider
    66	
    67	The simplest use case: redirect an existing provider through a proxy.
    68	
    69	```typescript
    70	// All Anthropic requests now go through your proxy
    71	pi.registerProvider("anthropic", {
    72	  baseUrl: "https://proxy.example.com"
    73	});
    74	
    75	// Add custom headers to OpenAI requests
    76	pi.registerProvider("openai", {
    77	  headers: {
    78	    "X-Custom-Header": "value"
    79	  }
    80	});
    81	
    82	// Both baseUrl and headers
    83	pi.registerProvider("google", {
    84	  baseUrl: "https://ai-gateway.corp.com/google",
    85	  headers: {
    86	    "X-Corp-Auth": "$CORP_AUTH_TOKEN"  // env var or literal
    87	  }
    88	});
    89	```
    90	
    91	When only `baseUrl` and/or `headers` are provided (no `models`), all existing models for that provider are preserved with the new endpoint.
    92	
    93	## Register New Provider
    94	
    95	To add a completely new provider, specify `models` along with the required configuration.

> AGENT

Yes, we can add a `wtg-openai` custom provider. And yes, your assumption is right: today there is no direct path for a Pi custom provider to read `base_url` from AgentV `targets.yaml`.

Current boundaries:

- Pi custom provider reads `baseUrl` from Pi config/extension.
- AgentV `pi-cli` target `base_url` is only wired for `subprovider: azure`.
- `subprovider: wtg-openai` will make AgentV call `pi --provider wtg-openai`.
- AgentV can pass the key via `--api-key`, but it will not pass a base URL.

Best options:

1. If the WTG endpoint can be committed or generated outside AgentV:
   Add Pi custom provider config, then use:

```yaml
- name: pi
  provider: pi-cli
  subprovider: wtg-openai
  api_key: ${{ OPENAI_API_KEY }}
  model: ${{ OPENAI_MODEL }}
  grader_target: grader
```

2. If the endpoint must come from env:
   Use a Pi extension/custom provider that reads something like `WTG_OPENAI_ENDPOINT`, not `OPENAI_ENDPOINT`, because AgentV’s `pi-cli` env filtering strips `OPENAI_*` when a custom subprovider is selected.

3. If we want this to be first-class in AgentV:
   Add AgentV core support to synthesize a temporary Pi custom provider from `targets.yaml` when `provider: pi-cli`, `subprovider: <custom>`, and `base_url` are set.

So: custom provider is viable, but `base_url` in `targets.yaml` won’t drive it without an AgentV core change or an upstream Pi `--base-url` feature.

> DEVELOPER

seems like best workaround is to use Azure for CLI  . perhaps we should document this in agentv docs.

> AGENT

I’ll add a narrow docs note rather than changing behavior: Pi SDK supports OpenAI-compatible `base_url` directly, while Pi CLI needs Azure mode or a preconfigured Pi custom provider for custom endpoints.

```yaml
targets:
  - name: copilot
    provider: copilot
    model: gpt-5-mini
    grader_target: azure-base
```

| Field | Required | Description |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| `model` | No | Model to use (defaults to copilot's default) |
| `cwd` | No | Working directory |
| `subprovider` | No | OpenAI-compatible provider type for `copilot`, `copilot-cli`, or `copilot-sdk`, such as `openai` or `azure` |
| `base_url` | No | Provider base URL or Azure resource URL/name |
| `api_key` | No | Provider API key. Prefer `${{ ENV_VAR }}` references. |
| `bearer_token` | No | Provider bearer token. Prefer `${{ ENV_VAR }}` references. Takes precedence over `api_key` when set. |
| `api_version` | No | Provider API version, primarily for Azure endpoints |
| `wire_api` | No | Provider wire API format, such as `responses` |
| `grader_target` | Yes | LLM target for evaluation |

Route Copilot through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint:

```yaml
targets:
  - name: copilot-openai
    provider: copilot-cli
    subprovider: openai
    base_url: ${{ OPENAI_ENDPOINT }}
    api_key: ${{ OPENAI_API_KEY }}
    wire_api: ${{ COPILOT_PROVIDER_WIRE_API }}
    grader_target: azure-base
```

Values can come from environment variables through `${{ ... }}` interpolation. For `copilot-cli`, AgentV maps these flat fields to Copilot's documented provider environment variables before spawning `copilot`; omitted fields leave existing ambient `COPILOT_PROVIDER_*` values unchanged.

## Pi Coding Agent

```yaml
targets:
  - name: pi_target
    provider: pi-coding-agent
    subprovider: openai-codex
    model: gpt-5.5
    thinking: medium
    grader_target: azure-base
```

| Field | Required | Description |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| `subprovider` | No | Pi provider to use, such as `google`, `openai`, `openai-codex`, `azure`, `anthropic`, or `openrouter`. Defaults to Pi's default provider. |
| `model` | No | Model to use. For OpenAI subscription auth through Pi, use `subprovider: openai-codex` with a subscription model such as `gpt-5.5`. |
| `thinking` | No | Pi reasoning level: `off`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, or `xhigh`. Passed to the Pi SDK as `thinkingLevel`. |
| `tools` | No | Comma-separated Pi tool allowlist, such as `read,bash,edit,write`. |
| `api_key` | No | Provider API key. Prefer `${{ ENV_VAR }}` references. Omit for subscription auth handled by Pi. |
| `base_url` | No | Provider base URL or Azure resource URL/name. |
| `cwd` | No | Working directory |
| `timeout_seconds` | No | Per-case timeout |
| `grader_target` | Yes | LLM target for evaluation |

Use `provider: pi-cli` instead when you want AgentV to spawn the `pi` binary directly. It accepts the same Pi fields above plus:

| Field | Required | Description |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| `executable` | No | Pi binary or shim to run. Defaults to `pi`. |
| `args` | No | Extra arguments appended before the prompt. |

## VS Code

```yaml
targets:
  - name: vscode_dev
    provider: vscode
    grader_target: azure-base
```

| Field | Required | Description |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| `executable` | No | Path to VS Code binary. Supports `${{ ENV_VAR }}` syntax or literal paths. Defaults to `code` (or `code-insiders` for the insiders provider). |
| `grader_target` | Yes | LLM target for evaluation |


```

## Claude

```yaml
targets:
  - name: claude_agent
    provider: claude
    grader_target: azure-base
```

| Field           | Required | Description                                                                                                                               |
| --------------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `executable`    | No       | CLI binary name or path (default: `claude`). Accepts a bare name looked up on PATH (e.g. `claude-zai`) or an absolute/relative file path. |
| `cwd`           | No       | Working directory                                                                                                                         |
| `grader_target` | Yes      | LLM target for evaluation                                                                                                                 |

## cc-mirror

[cc-mirror](https://github.com/numman-ali/cc-mirror) creates isolated Claude Code variants that route through alternative providers (Z.ai, Kimi, MiniMax, OpenRouter, etc.). The `cc-mirror` provider alias resolves to `claude-cli` and auto-discovers the binary path from `~/.cc-mirror/<variant>/variant.json`.

```yaml
targets:
  # Explicit variant with known executable
  - name: claude-zai
    provider: cc-mirror
    executable: claude-zai
    grader_target: azure-base

  # Auto-discover binary from variant.json
  - name: my-kimi
    provider: cc-mirror
    grader_target: azure-base
```

| Field           | Required | Description                                                                                                                            |
| --------------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `executable`    | No       | CLI binary name or path. When set, used directly (skips variant.json lookup).                                                          |
| `variant`       | No       | Variant name (directory under `~/.cc-mirror/`). Defaults to target `name`. Used to locate `variant.json` when `executable` is not set. |
| `cwd`           | No       | Working directory                                                                                                                      |
| `grader_target` | Yes      | LLM target for evaluation                                                                                                              |

Setup a variant first, then reference it by name:

```bash
npx cc-mirror quick --provider zai --name claude-zai --api-key "$Z_AI_API_KEY"
```

Since `cc-mirror` resolves to `claude-cli`, all Claude target fields (model, system_prompt, timeout_seconds, etc.) are also supported.

## Codex CLI

```yaml
targets:
  - name: codex_target
    provider: codex
    executable: codex-eng
    model: ${{ CODEX_MODEL }}
    model_reasoning_effort: ${{ CODEX_REASONING_EFFORT }}
    grader_target: azure-base
```

| Field                    | Required | Description                                                                |
| ------------------------ | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `executable`             | No       | Codex binary or profile shim to run, such as `codex-eng`                   |
| `model`                  | No       | Model to use                                                               |
| `model_reasoning_effort` | No       | Codex SDK reasoning effort: `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, or `xhigh` |
| `cwd`                    | No       | Working directory                                                          |
| `grader_target`          | Yes      | LLM target for evaluation                                                  |

## Copilot CLI

```yaml
targets:
  - name: copilot
    provider: copilot
    model: gpt-5-mini
    grader_target: azure-base
```

| Field           | Required | Description                                                                                                 |
| --------------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `model`         | No       | Model to use (defaults to copilot's default)                                                                |
| `cwd`           | No       | Working directory                                                                                           |
| `subprovider`   | No       | OpenAI-compatible provider type for `copilot`, `copilot-cli`, or `copilot-sdk`, such as `openai` or `azure` |
| `base_url`      | No       | Provider base URL or Azure resource URL/name                                                                |
| `api_key`       | No       | Provider API key. Prefer `${{ ENV_VAR }}` references.                                                       |
| `bearer_token`  | No       | Provider bearer token. Prefer `${{ ENV_VAR }}` references. Takes precedence over `api_key` when set.        |
| `api_version`   | No       | Provider API version, primarily for Azure endpoints                                                         |
| `wire_api`      | No       | Provider wire API format, such as `responses`                                                               |
| `grader_target` | Yes      | LLM target for evaluation                                                                                   |

Route Copilot through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint:

```yaml
targets:
  - name: copilot-openai
    provider: copilot-cli
    subprovider: openai
    base_url: ${{ OPENAI_ENDPOINT }}
    api_key: ${{ OPENAI_API_KEY }}
    wire_api: ${{ COPILOT_PROVIDER_WIRE_API }}
    grader_target: azure-base
```

Values can come from environment variables through `${{ ... }}` interpolation. For `copilot-cli`, AgentV maps these flat fields to Copilot's documented provider environment variables before spawning `copilot`; omitted fields leave existing ambient `COPILOT_PROVIDER_*` values unchanged.

## Pi Coding Agent

```yaml
targets:
  - name: pi_target
    provider: pi-coding-agent
    subprovider: openai-codex
    model: gpt-5.5
    thinking: medium
    grader_target: azure-base
```

| Field             | Required | Description                                                                                                                               |
| ----------------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `subprovider`     | No       | Pi provider to use, such as `google`, `openai`, `openai-codex`, `azure`, `anthropic`, or `openrouter`. Defaults to Pi's default provider. |
| `model`           | No       | Model to use. For OpenAI subscription auth through Pi, use `subprovider: openai-codex` with a subscription model such as `gpt-5.5`.       |
| `thinking`        | No       | Pi reasoning level: `off`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, or `xhigh`. Passed to the Pi SDK as `thinkingLevel`.                       |
| `tools`           | No       | Comma-separated Pi tool allowlist, such as `read,bash,edit,write`.                                                                        |
| `api_key`         | No       | Provider API key. Prefer `${{ ENV_VAR }}` references. Omit for subscription auth handled by Pi.                                           |
| `base_url`        | No       | Provider base URL or Azure resource URL/name.                                                                                             |
| `cwd`             | No       | Working directory                                                                                                                         |
| `timeout_seconds` | No       | Per-case timeout                                                                                                                          |
| `grader_target`   | Yes      | LLM target for evaluation                                                                                                                 |

For `provider: pi-coding-agent`, `base_url` is passed through the Pi SDK model
configuration. This works for OpenAI-compatible endpoints:

```yaml
targets:
  - name: pi-sdk-openai
    provider: pi-coding-agent
    subprovider: openai
    base_url: ${{ OPENAI_ENDPOINT }}
    api_key: ${{ OPENAI_API_KEY }}
    model: ${{ OPENAI_MODEL }}
    grader_target: azure-base
```

Use `provider: pi-cli` instead when you want AgentV to spawn the `pi` binary directly. It accepts the same Pi fields above plus:

| Field        | Required | Description                                 |
| ------------ | -------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| `executable` | No       | Pi binary or shim to run. Defaults to `pi`. |
| `args`       | No       | Extra arguments appended before the prompt. |

Pi CLI has one important difference from the SDK path: the built-in `openai`
provider does not currently expose a CLI base-url option. With `provider: pi-cli`
and `subprovider: openai`, AgentV can pass the API key and model, but `base_url`
does not re-route the built-in OpenAI provider. For custom endpoints, either
configure a Pi custom provider in Pi's own `models.json` and reference that
provider name as `subprovider`, or use Pi's Azure provider path when your gateway
is compatible with Azure OpenAI Responses:

```yaml
targets:
  - name: pi-cli-gateway
    provider: pi-cli
    subprovider: azure
    base_url: ${{ OPENAI_ENDPOINT }}
    api_key: ${{ OPENAI_API_KEY }}
    model: ${{ OPENAI_MODEL }}
    grader_target: azure-base
```

## VS Code

```yaml
targets:
  - name: vscode_dev
    provider: vscode
    grader_target: azure-base
```

| Field           | Required | Description                                                                                                                                   |
| --------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `executable`    | No       | Path to VS Code binary. Supports `${{ ENV_VAR }}` syntax or literal paths. Defaults to `code` (or `code-insiders` for the insiders provider). |
| `grader_target` | Yes      | LLM target for evaluation                                                                                                                     |

Using a custom executable path:

```yaml
targets:
  - name: vscode_dev
    provider: vscode
    executable: ${{ VSCODE_CMD }}
    grader_target: azure-base
```

## VS Code Insiders

```yaml
targets:
  - name: vscode_insiders
    provider: vscode-insiders
    grader_target: azure-base
```

Same configuration as VS Code.

## Custom CLI Agent

Evaluate any command-line agent:

```yaml
targets:
  - name: local_agent
    provider: cli
    command: "python agent.py --prompt-file {PROMPT_FILE} --output {OUTPUT_FILE}"
    grader_target: azure-base
```

| Field           | Required | Description                                                                                                     |
| --------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `command`       | Yes      | Command to run. `{PROMPT}` is inline prompt text and `{PROMPT_FILE}` is a temp file path containing the prompt. |
| `cwd`           | No       | Working directory                                                                                               |
| `grader_target` | Yes      | LLM target for evaluation                                                                                       |

## Mock Provider

For testing the evaluation harness without calling real providers:

```yaml
targets:
  - name: mock_target
    provider: mock

```
